selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What basic chain of reasoning is presented through the examples of a book and a house?
questions.answer: A meaningful product points to an act that produced it, that act points to a title like writer or builder, the title points to qualities or skills, and those qualities require a real being who possesses them.

questions.question: Why are the examples of writing and building used in this passage?
questions.answer: They make the argument easier to grasp by using familiar human examples to show that actions, qualities, and skilled results do not exist by themselves.

questions.question: According to the passage, why can there not be a deed without a doer?
questions.answer: Because an action needs a real source that performs it; it cannot stand on its own.

questions.question: What is the difference between a name and an attribute in the argument?
questions.answer: A name is a title such as writer or builder, while an attribute is the skill or quality that makes that title meaningful, like the ability to write or build.

questions.question: What does the passage say about a craft and a craftsman?
questions.answer: A craft necessarily points to someone who practices and possesses it.

questions.question: How is the universe described after this principle is stated?
questions.answer: It is described as being like many meaningful writings and many carefully made structures.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare the universe both to books and to buildings?
questions.answer: The two comparisons highlight both meaning and structure: the universe is full of signs to be read and also shows order, design, and construction.

questions.question: What does “each of these singly in thousands of ways and together in uncountable ways” imply?
questions.answer: Every being gives many signs on its own, and when all beings are considered together, their witness becomes vastly stronger.

questions.question: What does the mention of Divine Power especially emphasize?
questions.answer: It emphasizes the actual bringing into existence and formation of things.

questions.question: How does the passage encourage a believer to view the natural world?
questions.answer: As a field of signs that direct the heart and mind to Allah’s real action, power, and wisdom.

questions.question: In this passage, what does a finely made book point to first?
questions.answer: It points first to the act of writing.

questions.question: What does a solidly made house point to first?
questions.answer: It points first to the act of building.

questions.question: After the act, what is the next level in the passage’s sequence?
questions.answer: The next level is the names or titles connected to the act, such as writer and builder.

questions.question: After names or titles, what further reality is required?
questions.answer: Skills and qualities that make those names true are required.

questions.question: After skills and qualities, what final reality must exist?
questions.answer: A real being who has those skills and qualities must exist.

questions.question: What principle is being established by this sequence?
questions.answer: Orderly works lead the mind step by step to an acting and qualified maker.

questions.question: How does this principle rule out the idea that attributes exist by themselves?
questions.answer: It says qualities cannot float independently; they must belong to someone.

questions.question: What view of the universe follows from this principle?
questions.answer: The universe is seen as a meaningful work full of signs of intentional making.

questions.question: What kind of relationship between all beings is implied by their joint testimony?
questions.answer: Their signs support one another and gather into one larger witness.

questions.question: What is the effect of combining the witness of all beings together?
questions.answer: Their combined witness becomes far greater than the witness of any one being alone.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the first sentence in the marked passage?
questions.answer: Produced things necessarily point beyond themselves to producing actions, qualities, and ultimately to a real producer.

questions.question: How does the passage move from visible objects to an unseen source?
questions.answer: It reasons from observed works to acts, from acts to names, from names to attributes, and from attributes to the being who possesses them.

questions.question: Why is this an argument from signs rather than from direct sight?
questions.answer: Because the maker is not being directly seen here; instead, the conclusion is drawn from the existence and character of the works.

questions.question: What role do “beautifully” and “well” play in the examples?
questions.answer: They show that the issue is not mere existence but skilled, purposeful, and orderly production.
